# Exact two-group accounting and the five-cap reserve
three-cap overlap coefficient. They identify the remaining geometric
sign; rewriting that sign is not progress toward proving it. The
unconditional sign route remains blocked without an additional premise.

## 1. Actual data and ownership

Let S have finitely many positive full two-dimensional convex fibers
K_z, with areas w_z and total M. Let two groups of distinct ORIGINAL
ambient closed caps cover, respectively, every fiber in an ownership
partition P=P_0 disjoint-union P_1. This may be the integer half-line
ownership supplied by two actual critical circuits. No cap is changed
when ownership is chosen. Assume every original cap appearing here has
the same global mixed mass B>0.

For cap i in group j write a_ji(z)=|K_z intersect H_ji|. Define

    X_j=sum_(i in group j) sum_(z notin P_j) a_ji(z).

Repeated original caps in different groups are counted with their
group occurrences. For a three-cap group define

    L_j=sum_(z in P_j) min_i a_ji(z),
    Delta_j=B-L_j,
    E_j=sum_(z in P_j)[sum_i a_ji(z)-w_z-(3/4)min_i a_ji(z)].

The audited ordinary effective-three-cap theorem gives E_j>=0,
including full and empty traces and arbitrary continuous-normal rank.
Also 0<=L_j<=B, since its summand is bounded by the trace of any one
fixed group cap and that cap's global mass is B. Thus Delta_j>=0.
For a two-cap group put

    E_j=sum_(z in P_j)[sum_i a_ji(z)-w_z]>=0.

This last quantity is the actual owned overlap. All boundaries are
retained; continuous facet boundaries are area-null, while a cap
constant on a fiber is treated as full or empty.

## 2. Two triples and shared original labels

For two groups of three caps, summing their owned identities gives

    M=(9/2)B-X+(3/4)(Delta_0+Delta_1)-E,                (1)
    X=X_0+X_1,  E=E_0+E_1.

Indeed their total owned cap mass is 6B-X, and
L_0+L_1=2B-(Delta_0+Delta_1). This proves (1) without assigning any
cap mass twice except where its group occurrence is explicitly counted.
The desired n=1,d=2 budget M<=(9/2)B would therefore follow from

    X+E >= (3/4)(Delta_0+Delta_1).                     (2)

No general proof of (2) is supplied here. The earlier genuine
one-group negative-credit example shows why deleting E is not
justified by criticality alone.

If the triples share exactly one original cap H, its contribution
to X is EXACTLY B: its outside-owned mass for the first group is
its mass on P_1, and that for the second is its mass on P_0. Thus

    X=B+X_unique,   X_unique>=0.                       (3)

It is incorrect either to discard this contribution or to count it
as two independent B budgets. Equations (1)--(3) retain its exact
value. If the triples share two or more caps, there are at most
four distinct caps; their ordinary union bound already gives
M<=4B<(9/2)B, without any profile estimate.

## 3. A triple and a pair: the exact B/4 reserve

For one triple (index3) and one pair (index2), with all five labels
distinct, the same direct summation gives

    M=(17/4)B-X+(3/4)Delta_3-E_3-E_2.                 (4)

Consequently the desired budget follows whenever

    X+E_3+E_2+B/4 >= (3/4)Delta_3.                   (5)

In particular it holds if Delta_3<=B/3, equivalently L_3>=2B/3,
since X,E_3,E_2 are nonnegative. The B/4 is an actual reserve from
the two-cap group, not an asymptotic constant. When these groups
share a label, at most four distinct caps remain and the union
bound again suffices. No claim that (5) holds automatically in the
remaining dispersion range is made.

## 4. Additional geometry at two actual deepest contacts

Suppose the two groups are genuine positive critical circuits at
actual deepest points over adjacent bases 0 and 1. Subtract the
affine interpolation of the two continuous contact coordinates.
This is one lattice-preserving fiber shear with continuous Jacobian
one. Every critical cap has nonpositive margin at every deepest
point, by the positive-slab contact argument. Therefore its new
margin has one of the forms

    u_0i dot x-c_i z,          c_i>=0,
    u_1i dot x+b_i(z-1),       b_i>=0.                 (6)

This is the proved two-contact normal form in
`candidate 1859dbfb4aa7eadc`, now applied to
actual deepest contacts. The signs hold for each cap separately.
At the formal continuous point x=0 the group0 margins are
nonnegative on z<=0 and the group1 margins are nonnegative on z>=1;
the opposite group's margins there are nonpositive, with strictness
only when the corresponding coefficient is positive. A cap shared
by the two groups has c_i=b_i=0 and passes through x=0 at every
real base, because its affine margin vanishes at both contacts.

No source fiber outside [0,1] is assumed to contain continuous0.
That pointwise membership does not follow from (6). Actual source
fibers still satisfy the usual Minkowski inclusions, but no estimate
combining these inclusions with (6) to prove (2) or (5) is established
here. In particular an angular radialization based on source bodies
containing zero on every owned base would add an unsupported premise.

The geometric compensation step is left explicitly unresolved, not
promoted to a lemma. These identities preserve the correct original
cap, ownership, and shared-label data for a future new mechanism.
